article.title: Week 1 Recap
body: There are a lot of respectable ways to lose a fantasy football game. You can score 140 and run into the one person who scored 145. You can lose a starting running back in the first quarter. You can spend four months researching dynasty football and then discover around 4:15 on Sunday that everything you believed was wrong. jtyurconic2 decided none of those were sufficiently interesting, so he started Josh Allen and Derrick Henry, received 70.46 fantasy points and seven actual touchdowns from the two of them, and lost 122.87 to 121.06.

Allen threw for 334 yards, ran for two touchdowns and became the first quarterback in NFL history to reach 80 career rushing scores. Henry ran for 144 yards and three touchdowns. Most 32-year-old running backs are supposed to be discussing veteran leadership while somebody younger gets 14 carries. Henry got 24 and averaged six yards a pop. Sleeper says jtyurconic2's optimal lineup would have scored 148.86. dball11's would have scored 159.08. Between them, the two managers left 64.01 potential points sitting around unused, which makes the 1.81-point final margin feel less like a classic duel and more like two guys trying to assemble IKEA furniture without admitting they threw away the instructions.

dackerly36 had a different problem. Caleb Williams scored 37.26 and Justin Jefferson scored 27.2, which gave him 64.46 points from two starters and 35.30 from the other eight combined. One of those eight scored negative 0.1. Another scored zero. I had initially thought 99.76 was an impressively low total until I remembered that Chicago and Carolina combined for 96 actual NFL points on Sunday, the most ever in an NFL season opener. Caleb accounted for 334 yards and four touchdowns while the Bears scored 59, their highest total in an opener in franchise history. So for one afternoon an entire professional football game nearly caught dackerly's fantasy team, which is not a comparison I expected to have available in Week 1.
Hank1517 beat him 123.40 to 99.76 and can mostly be credited with having the good sense to stand on the other side.

Taylor Swift skipped the Emmys for Arrowhead Monday night. TheBearJew44 had a less culturally significant but probably more urgent reason to be watching Kansas City. Kyler Murray, one of his two starting quarterbacks, completed three passes for 18 yards before leaving Minnesota's opener with a concussion and finished with 0.62 fantasy points. Ordinarily this would be the sort of development that ruins a superflex lineup before the late games have even started. Kenneth Walker III apparently disagreed. In his first game with Kansas City, Walker ran for a career-high 173 yards, finished with 191 yards from scrimmage and scored twice, including a 60-yard touchdown. TheBearJew44 beat connordolan14 145.26 to 134.69 despite getting less than one fantasy point from a starting quarterback, which is roughly the fantasy equivalent of making it home before noticing somewhere around Delaware that one of your tires is missing.

ryanog was considerably less theatrical. He scored a league-high 153.60 against greenie0513's 117.90 without having a single starter reach 30 points. Five different starters scored between 22.2 and 26.1. This is irritating in the same way that watching somebody calmly finish a group project three days early is irritating. There is nothing obvious to make fun of, everybody did his job, and somehow the whole thing is sitting in your inbox while you are still deciding what font to use.

BrendanBall03 had the other major score, beating jbitterman99 148.13 to 123.71, while chrisrenna17 beat mhaanders 134.35 to 100.04. mhaanders deserves a small amount of recognition for setting a lineup with a potential score of 100.94 and producing 100.04, meaning there was essentially nothing better hiding on the roster. Sometimes the machine really is just broken.
forTheRecord: Derrick Henry finished Sunday with 125 career rushing touchdowns, passing Marcus Allen for third in NFL history. More absurdly, 110 of his 144 rushing yards came before contact, the third-highest total of his career, and Indianapolis managed to hit him at the line on only 8.3% of his carries.

ryanog posted the highest score in the league while leaving Bryce Young's 32.44 points on the bench. Young threw for 361 yards against Chicago. Apparently 153.60 was the conservative version of the lineup.

Kenneth Walker's 191 yards from scrimmage were the most ever in Week 1 by a reigning Super Bowl MVP, passing Jerry Rice's 180 in 1989. His 173 rushing yards were also the second-most by any veteran making his debut with a new team, behind Michael Turner's 220-yard Falcons debut in 2008. Apparently changing employers went fine.

article.title: Week 2 Recap
body: At the end of Week 1, dackerly36 had 99.76 points and what seemed like a fairly secure claim to the league’s most embarrassing performance. A normal person might have spent the next seven days figuring out how to improve. dackerly36 apparently spent them figuring out how to divide by two.

He scored 49.97 this week. Exactly half of last week’s total would have been 49.88, so he overshot the target by nine hundredths of a point, possibly out of respect for the rest of us. Nobody in his starting lineup reached double digits. Harold Fannin led the way with 9.15, and Caleb Williams managed 8.72 as Chicago followed its 59-point opener by scoring three against Minnesota. It was a difficult week for the Bears offense, but at least the Bears only had to be the Bears once.

dball11 won 143.27 to 49.97, a margin of 93.30. For perspective, Josh Allen scored 40.82 for jtyurconic2. Add Fannin’s 9.15 and you have dackerly36’s entire team total, exactly. One quarterback and one tight end did the work of ten starters. If this is a deliberate rebuilding strategy, I’d be interested to know which part is under construction.

Allen, meanwhile, opened Buffalo’s new stadium by accounting for five touchdowns against Detroit, which is the sort of performance that usually makes a fantasy manager start composing an obnoxious group-chat message before the Sunday games have even kicked off. jtyurconic2 probably considered it. He’d already lost in Week 1 despite getting 70.46 combined points from Allen and Derrick Henry, so surely 40.82 from Allen alone would buy him a little peace.

Unfortunately, ryanog had Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and Seattle’s backup quarterback apparently had no interest in honoring the normal expectations for backup quarterbacks. Drew Lock’s first pass to Smith-Njigba wasn’t even supposed to be a deep route; Smith-Njigba got so open that Lock threw it 82 yards for a touchdown anyway. He finished with nine catches, 155 yards and three scores. ryanog put up a league-high 165.79 and beat jtyurconic2’s 130.55. Two weeks into the season, Josh Allen is 2-0 in real life and his fantasy manager is 0-2. There may be a lesson about team sports here, although it seems unnecessarily cruel to make him learn it twice.

The week’s most useful celebrity news came from Beverly Hills, where Puka Nacua spent the weekend judging a chicken-tender competition alongside Lizzo. Nacua missed Monday’s Rams game with a hip injury, leaving Davante Adams to catch eight passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns. chrisrenna17 had Adams and Matthew Stafford, who combined for 63.48 fantasy points, and beat Hank1517 125.28 to 88.62 despite getting 0.8 from Jaxson Dart. If there is a connection between celebrity chicken judging and chrisrenna17’s win, I’m not qualified to establish it. I am qualified to suggest that he send Lizzo a thank-you note.

Elsewhere, mhaanders edged jbitterman99 134.45 to 132.40, TheBearJew44 beat BrendanBall03 145.98 to 127.03, and connordolan14 defeated greenie0513 93.88 to 88.00. That last result is a nice reminder that fantasy football remains a fair and sensible enterprise: 93.88 was enough to win, while 132.40 wasn’t. jbitterman99 is now 0-2 with 256.11 points scored. I’d tell him to keep doing what he’s doing, but he might reasonably ask me to go fuck myself.
forTheRecord: Davante Adams gained more receiving yards by himself than the Giants gained on offense. Adams had 195; New York had 182 total.

Christian McCaffrey’s 100 career touchdowns are split perfectly between his two teams: 50 with Carolina and 50 with San Francisco. Even stranger, he scored exactly 32 rushing touchdowns and 18 receiving touchdowns for each franchise.

Aaron Donald returned to an NFL field Monday for the first time in 982 days. The Rams brought him back after more than two years away; dackerly36 might want to ask whether retirement is available to fantasy rosters as well.

article.title: Week 3 Recap
body: Three weeks into a fantasy season is enough time for everyone to become completely unreasonable. Nobody with a winning record thinks three games is a small sample. Everybody with a losing record does. The people in the middle have already opened a trade calculator 45 times and convinced themselves they are one flex upgrade away.
So yes, it is still early. The New York Mudbones are also making that increasingly difficult to care about.

The Mudbones scored 176.55 this week after putting up 153.60 and 165.79 in the first two. That is three straight weeks as the highest-scoring team in the league. Jaxon Smith-Njigba added another 30.36 after scoring 38 last week, and nine of the ten starters finished in double figures. If every team played every other team each week, New York Mudbones would currently be 33-0.
The Permanent Rebuild scored 73.95 on the other side. Anyway.

Green Egbukas & Ham finally won, and did it convincingly, beating Hanging With Hernandez 143.38 to 102.96. Jahmyr Gibbs scored 37.9, Brock Bowers returned with 25.1, and Green Egbukas went from looking completely dead through two weeks to putting up the third-highest score of Week 3.

This was also a big weekend nationally for learning how to celebrate a good performance. Texas defensive end Colin Simmons tied the school record with five sacks against Tennessee, then celebrated one of them by pretending to unzip his pants and piss on the field. The officials announced the penalty as “simulating using the restroom,” which is such a polite description of the event that it sounds like Simmons was asking permission to leave a third-grade classroom. Green Egbukas won by 40 and, as far as I know, everybody kept their pants on.

Team chrisrenna17 is now sitting second in the standings after beating Woodys Toy Box 142.31 to 96.01. Bijan Robinson did most of the damage with 34.3, rushing for 194 yards against Green Bay. The Packers on the other hand rushed for 17, just enough to still be eligible for a trip to Epstein's Island. BrendanBall03 also had a good week, beating Injured Reserve 145.72 to 134.30. Injured Reserve actually finished fifth in league scoring and still lost, so the top-six bonus at least provided the fantasy equivalent of the airline giving you 5,000 miles after losing your luggage. BrendanBall03 got 31.28 from Brock Purdy, who threw four touchdowns in San Francisco’s win.

New England Keys beat Team jtyurconic2 134.16 to 117.70 and finished exactly sixth in weekly scoring, grabbing the final top-half bonus. Team jtyurconic2 is now 0.5-4 despite having scored 369.31 points, which is more than five teams currently ahead of it in the standings. There is probably an argument to be made here about strength of schedule. Unfortunately fantasy football has never shown much interest in your argument.
Mark 2.0 picked up its first head-to-head win of the season as well, beating It Hurts When I Pitts 125.58 to 90.27.

So after three weeks, New York Mudbones is 4.5-0, Team chrisrenna17 is 4-0.5, BrendanBall03 is 3-1.5, and the middle of the standings is already becoming the kind of place where everybody can find one statistic proving they are actually better than their record.
This is usually how it starts.

The teams at the top decide the standings are finally telling the truth. The teams at the bottom start talking about points against. Everybody else discovers that their bench would apparently be a playoff team if only they had the courage to start it.
Three weeks ago, everyone liked their roster. Give it another two and somebody is going to trade a future first because they are “one piece away.”
forTheRecord: Jaxon Smith-Njigba entered the NFL with questions about whether he was basically a slot receiver. Through three games this season, 365 of his 405 receiving yards and five of his six touchdowns have come while lined up outside. He currently leads the NFL in catches, yards and touchdowns from a wide alignment.

Jahmyr Gibbs became the first player in NFL history with at least 300 rushing yards, four rushing touchdowns, 150 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns through the first three games of a season. He also passed Billy Sims for second on Detroit's career rushing-touchdown list. Gibbs is 24.

Bijan Robinson ran for 194 yards Thursday night. Drake London had exactly 194 receiving yards in the same game. It was already the third time the two have each gone over 150 yards from scrimmage in the same game, more than any pair of teammates in NFL history.

Deebo Samuel finished Sunday with zero receptions, 80 receiving yards and a touchdown. Mike Evans caught a Brock Purdy pass and lateraled it to Deebo, who took it the rest of the way. Evans got the catch. Deebo got the 80 receiving yards. Somewhere there is a statistician who had to explain this to his boss.

article.title: Week 4 Recap
body: Week 4 was a pretty good argument against the idea that fantasy football rewards the best team. The New York Mudbones had the third-highest score in the league and lost. Injured Reserve was one of three teams that failed to break 90 and won. One of those managers has every reason to complain about the schedule this week, while the other should probably avoid bringing it up.

Team chrisrenna17 deserves the credit for the Mudbones’ first loss because it wasn’t exactly a collapse. The Mudbones still scored 152.39, which would have comfortably beaten almost everyone else. Team chrisrenna17 just happened to have Tetairoa McMillan score 38.2 while the rest of the lineup did enough to get to 162.95. That puts Team chrisrenna17 on top of the standings after four weeks, although I imagine the Mudbones will be filing an appeal based on the fact that they would still be 42-2 if we made everyone play everybody.

The New England Keys were actually the highest-scoring team this week with 163.40, which was a fairly impressive group effort considering nine starters scored in double figures and none scored 30. Their opponent was The Permanent Rebuild, which scored 64.30. I have been asked to stop making the same joke about this team every week and, luckily, a 99-point loss has removed most of the need for additional commentary.

Green Egbukas & Ham made it two straight wins by beating Team BrendanBall03 145.02 to 112.65. This might have been the least stressful lineup in the league all weekend. Eight starters reached double figures, nobody scored more than 25.5, and there was never a point where the entire outcome depended on one guy catching a screen pass on Monday night. Fantasy analysts would probably call this “depth.” I would call it a nice way to spend a Sunday.

Hanging With Hernandez beat Team jtyurconic2 behind 30.4 from Kenneth Walker III and 28.8 from Javonte Williams. Five rushing touchdowns between the two of them should normally create a little more separation than this. Team jtyurconic2 took a pounding from Hanging With Hernandez but somehow stayed within 5.83.
Mark 2.0 won the closest matchup of the week behind 32.8 from CeeDee Lamb and 31.7 from Kyren Williams. Woodys Toy Box got worked from behind late and couldn’t hold on, losing 131.73 to 128.02.

Then there was Injured Reserve beating It Hurts When I Pitts 86.47 to 67.85, a game that I was prepared to criticize until I saw what the Minnesota Vikings have been doing. Minnesota is 4-0 despite already winning two games this season without scoring a touchdown. Only two other teams in NFL history have ever started 4-0 while failing to score a touchdown in two of those games, and both were the Chicago Cardinals in the early 1920s, when a significant portion of the league probably still considered the forward pass a fad and beer was still illegal.
So I’m temporarily suspending the idea that a win has to look good.
Injured Reserve started ten players, got 86 points and left with the result it needed. The Vikings have apparently established legal precedent.

That brings us through the first month of the season, which is usually where the preseason version of everyone’s roster finally starts getting replaced by the one that actually exists. Team chrisrenna17 is sitting at the top, the Mudbones finally lost a game, Green Egbukas & Ham has won two straight, and several teams that looked either great or completely hopeless two weeks ago have already changed the argument.
September is mostly for explaining why you were right about your team. October is when other people start getting evidence.
forTheRecord: Tetairoa McMillan had 14 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns Sunday. In the first three games of the season combined, he had 12 catches for 193 yards and zero touchdowns. He essentially recreated his entire September in one night and missed the yardage total by one.

CeeDee Lamb caught 17 passes for 189 yards and the game-winning touchdown with 40 seconds left. He became only the fourth player in NFL history with at least 17 catches, 180 receiving yards and a touchdown in the same game, joining Tom Fears, Terrell Owens and Brandon Marshall.

Kenneth Walker III has now rushed for at least 170 yards twice in Kansas City’s first four games. The only other players in NFL history to do that twice within a team’s first four games are Jim Brown and O.J. Simpson.

Kyle Monangai carried the ball 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets. Chicago finished the game with 34 first downs. The Jets ran 32 offensive plays. The Bears literally earned more first downs than New York had opportunities to snap the football.

rulebook.html:
1. League Structure

  1. The league consists of 12 teams.
  2. The league has no divisions.
  3. Six teams qualify for the playoffs.
  4. The top two playoff seeds receive first-round byes.

2. Entry Fee and Prizes

  1. The annual entry fee is $150 per team.
  2. The standard prize pool will be distributed as follows:
    • First place: $900
    • Second place: $500
    • Third place: $250
    • Fourth place: $150
  3. Each week, the team with the lowest point total in its starting lineup must contribute an additional $10 to a separate prize pool.
  4. After the postseason, the separate prize pool will be distributed as follows:
    • Fifth place: $90
    • Sixth place: $50

3. Rosters and Lineups

  1. Each team has a 25-player active roster consisting of:
    • 10 starting-lineup spots
    • 15 bench spots
  2. Each team also has three taxi-squad spots. Taxi spots are separate from the 25-player active roster.
  3. The taxi-squad deadline is the start of the NFL regular season.
  4. Each starting lineup consists of:
    • One quarterback
    • Two running backs
    • Two wide receivers
    • One tight end
    • Three flex players
    • One superflex player
  5. The league does not use kickers or team defense/special teams.

4. Scoring Format

  1. The league uses half-point PPR scoring.
  2. Tight ends receive an additional 0.25 points per reception.
  3. Each tight-end reception is therefore worth 0.75 points total.

5. Waivers and Free Agency

  1. The league uses FAAB waivers.
  2. Each team receives a $1,000 FAAB budget.
  3. Bids of $0 are allowed.
  4. In-season waivers process at 3:00 a.m. each Wednesday.
  5. A player who is released remains on waivers for two days before becoming a free agent.

6. Regular Season and Playoffs

  1. The regular-season schedule will be randomized each year.
  2. Each week, the six teams with the highest point totals receive an additional 0.5 wins.
  3. The additional 0.5 wins are separate from the results of the teams’ scheduled head-to-head matchups.
  4. After each playoff round, the remaining teams will be reseeded.
  5. The highest remaining seed will play the lowest remaining seed.

7. Trades

  1. Trading is allowed during the regular season and offseason.
  2. Trading is not allowed during the playoffs.
  3. All managers participating in a trade must agree to the trade before the first snap of the first NFL game of Week 15.
  4. All trades are subject to league review.
  5. A trade will be vetoed only if at least 75% of the league’s members vote to reject it.
  6. In a 12-team league, 75% of the full league membership equals nine managers.
  7. If a manager trades away a future first-round rookie pick, that manager must promptly pay the entry fee for the season in which the pick will be used.

8. Rookie Draft

  1. The rookie draft consists of four rounds.
  2. The rookie draft uses a linear format. The draft order remains the same in every round and does not reverse between rounds.
  3. Each selection has a two-minute time limit.

Non-Playoff Teams: Picks 1–6

  1. The six teams that do not qualify for the playoffs receive rookie draft positions 1 through 6.
  2. Those teams are ordered by regular-season Maximum Points For, from lowest to highest.
  3. The non-playoff team with the lowest Max PF receives draft position 1.
  4. The non-playoff team with the highest Max PF receives draft position 6.

Playoff Teams: Picks 7–12

  1. The six playoff teams receive rookie draft positions 7 through 12 based on their regular-season playoff seeds.
  2. The order is:
    • Sixth seed: Draft position 7
    • Fifth seed: Draft position 8
    • Fourth seed: Draft position 9
    • Third seed: Draft position 10
    • Second seed: Draft position 11
    • First seed: Draft position 12
  3. Postseason results do not change the rookie draft positions of playoff teams.
  4. For example, a team that enters the playoffs as the fifth seed receives draft position 8, even if that team later wins the league championship.

9. Offseason Waivers

  1. During the offseason, waivers process on Tuesdays.
  2. After Tuesday waivers process, unclaimed players become free agents for the remainder of Tuesday.
  3. Player-add transactions are locked for the remainder of the week.
  4. Offseason waiver claims use the same FAAB budget as the rest of the season.

10. Rule Changes

  1. New rules may be proposed during the offseason.
  2. A proposed rule may be submitted in the league group chat or directly to the commissioner.
  3. The league will discuss each proposed rule before voting on it.

11. Startup Draft

  1. The startup draft consists of 28 rounds.

Pick Times

  1. Rounds 1 through 5 have a two-minute time limit per pick.
  2. Rounds 6 through 20 have a three-minute time limit per pick.
  3. Rounds 21 through 28 have a two-minute time limit per pick.

Trading Timeouts

  1. Each manager receives five total minutes of draft-pause time to discuss trades.
  2. A manager may use the five minutes all at once or divide them among multiple timeouts.

Conversion to a Slow Draft

  1. If the startup draft is not completed on the scheduled draft day, the remaining selections will convert to a slow draft.
  2. The slow draft begins when the in-person portion of the draft ends.
  3. The slow draft continues until the day before the NFL regular season begins.
  4. There is no formal time limit for an individual selection during the slow draft.
  5. Managers are expected to make their selections promptly and keep the draft moving.
